description: Agent Bookkeeping: submit a general-ledger extract with the source totals it should agree with: the extract with its reference, the business it belongs to, its currency, each suspense or clearing account the books keep, and each posting line with its id, entry number, posting date, the period it posts to, the account, its debit or credit, its memo and the source document it posts; the source totals with their currency and each total with the account, the period and its debit and credit totals, such as a trial balance or subledger. The signed report gives the extract and the sources, each period’s debits against its credits, each source document or dated memo posted again to the same account in another entry, the gaps in each run of entry numbers, the balance left in each suspense or clearing account at the end of the extract, and each account’s ledger total against its source total, and counts them, and names a divergent ledger: a period whose debits and credits differ, a duplicate posting of the same document, a sequence gap in the entry numbering, residue left in a suspense account, and an account total unlike its source total; then source totals in another currency and a line dated outside the month it posts to, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No posting lines, no debits or credits, no source documents or memos, no entry numbers, no suspense account named or recognizable, or no source totals leaves those points unverified. Amounts compare to the cent, accounts by their number where both carry one and otherwise by their words with plurals folded, and entry numbers as a prefix and a running number. This reads a business’s accounting books: wever_agent-permission-ledger keeps a permission record of the grants and revocations an agent’s actions are checked against, while the ledger check reads the general ledger a business keeps of its own transactions. Verdict bookkeeping_ledger_divergent, bookkeeping_ledger_partial, bookkeeping_ledger_unverified or bookkeeping_ledger_consistent. POST /api/bookkeeping-ledger-check. Reads the bookkeeping records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the books as supplied only: it never posts or edits an entry, never moves money or pays a bill, never files anything with any authority and gives no tax advice, which stay with the business, its bookkeeper and its advisers, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Bookkeeping reads a business’s own books for internal consistency and against the records they should agree with: a general-ledger extract, a bank reconciliation, journal entries, a chart of accounts, a period close, the accounts payable ledger, a payroll register and the accounts receivable ledger, each against its own debits and credits, the source totals supplied, the bank statement and the ledger balance, the open period, the posting queue and recurring entries, or the ledger postings and pay schedule it should agree with. The family reads bookkeeping, the record a business keeps of its own transactions in its ledger and journals, and reads the records against each other. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-bookkeeping-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-bookkeeping/.
